When kinetic energy is conserved.
When total momentum before equals total after.
When masses are equal.

questions.explanation: Momentum conservation requires equal totals before and after. Energy and speed patterns are separate.

questions.topic: Kinetic energy error in inelastic collision
questions.stem: Biologist Sam reviews a field note claiming KE is conserved in a sticking collision and asks the error.

options.text: Sticking collisions conserve only potential energy.
Sticking collisions conserve kinetic energy.
Sticking collisions create kinetic energy.
Sticking collisions lose kinetic energy.

questions.explanation: Sticking collisions are perfectly inelastic and lose KE. Momentum is conserved instead.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.stem: Biologist Tia asks why a padded collar reduces force on a tracked animal.

options.text: It reduces total impulse delivered.
It extends impact time for fixed impulse.
It eliminates momentum change.
It increases peak force.

questions.explanation: Padding extends duration, lowering peak force for fixed impulse. This protects the animal.
